text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 use concentrated on low-complexity patients is consistent with upcoding, but records are too thin to confirm it.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The claims pattern points toward upcoding rather than a sicker panel. The 99215 share runs above the all-provider rate in every complexity band, and most of this provider's 99215s fall on patients with zero or one chronic condition. Sampled examples such as C0112208 and C0112725 (J06.9 upper respiratory infection, no chronic conditions) and C0112274 (N39.0) show the highest code on what look like routine acute visits, while high-complexity examples like C0112234 fit a level-5 visit. The documentation cannot settle the question: only one 99215 claim was reviewed (C0112125, supported at high MDM), and the few below-billed findings at 99213 and 99214 come from very small counts, so the records neither confirm nor rule out the claims-based signal. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, especially the acute-diagnosis visits, and check whether the notes support high MDM or are templated, given that one moderate-plus data-reviewed note had no lab or test line on the claim."}
